profile.summary: I build systems where language models do real work reliably: a provider-agnostic multi-agent platform, a financial advisor that computes figures instead of generating them, and a retrieval-augmented tutor running in production for a real coaching academy. Full-stack and database work rounds out the toolkit — the AI engineering is the point.

about: I'm a third-year computer science student specializing in artificial intelligence. Most of my work sits at the applied end of AI engineering: taking language models beyond a chat window and into systems with orchestration, retrieval, guardrails, and observability — and shipping them on real cloud infrastructure.

What I care about is the engineering judgment around the model: when to let an LLM decide and when to force a deterministic path, how to keep providers swappable, and how to make an agent's behaviour visible and debuggable rather than magical.

featured_projects.title: Enterprise Multi-Agent AI Platform
featured_projects.oneliner: A provider-agnostic, cloud-native platform for hosting multiple collaborating AI agents — agents, LLM providers, memory, tools, search, and vector stores are each replaceable through configuration, without touching business logic.

sections.title: The problem
sections.body: Most agent projects hard-wire one vendor's SDK through the entire codebase, so swapping a model, a search backend, or a vector store means rewriting business logic. This platform treats every AI capability as a replaceable provider behind a typed interface.

sections.title: Architecture & key decisions
bullets: Five layers with strictly one-way dependencies; exactly one package is permitted to import a vendor SDK. Switching model families across Azure subscriptions cost three environment variables and zero code changes.

Keyless authentication throughout — DefaultAzureCredential locally and Managed Identity in Azure, with API keys disabled at the resource level (disableLocalAuth), so a leaked key is impossible rather than merely discouraged.

The agentic tool loop enforces budgets between iterations — maximum tool invocations and model calls are checked where stopping still saves the next call, so an unbounded loop cannot turn one request into an open-ended bill.
Tool usage is streamed to the UI as a dedicated SSE event, so a turn that searches the web is visibly an agent at work, and answers cite the search that produced them.
Full observability: structured JSON logging and OpenTelemetry tracing with a correlation ID propagated from HTTP request through runtime, providers, logs, and traces.

Delivery discipline: mypy --strict, 600+ tests at ~95% coverage, CI quality gates on every pull request, non-root Docker images with vulnerability scanning, and the complete Azure resource graph defined in Bicep.

featured_projects.title: FinPal — Student Financial Advisor
featured_projects.oneliner: Conversational financial advisor where the model handles conversation and a deterministic rules engine handles arithmetic — financial figures are computed, never generated.

sections.title: The problem
sections.body: Students asking an LLM for financial advice get numbers that sound right. An advisor is only trustworthy if its figures are actually right — every time.

sections.title: The central design decision
sections.body: LLM-driven dialogue is kept strictly separate from a deterministic, rules-based calculation engine. The model never produces a financial figure; it interprets the question and presents the answer, while the rules engine does the arithmetic. That separation covers budget allocation, investment projections, EMI affordability, debt payoff strategies, and emergency fund calculations.

sections.title: Architecture
bullets: Voice and text input: in-browser audio capture transcribed with Groq Whisper, replies streamed over Server-Sent Events.
Session persistence through the SQLAlchemy ORM on PostgreSQL/SQLite.
Provider-agnostic LLM layer across OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter, and Google Gemini.

featured_projects.role: Solo project — design and implementation end to end.

architecture.caption: Dialogue and arithmetic never share a layer: the LLM interprets and presents; the rules engine computes.

featured_projects.title: AI Virtual Tutor for a Coaching Academy
featured_projects.oneliner: Retrieval-augmented tutoring system for IIT-JAM exam preparation, built for a real coaching academy and running in production — with mandatory specialist-model routing for life-sciences questions.
highlights: In production for a real client

sections.title: The problem
sections.body: Students preparing for the IIT-JAM entrance exam need accurate answers grounded in their academy's own teaching material — including live-class transcripts spoken in mixed Marathi, Hindi, and English. This was built for a real client, not as a course exercise.

sections.title: Architecture & key decisions
bullets: An orchestrator model routes each question across specialist models, with a hard constraint: biotechnology and life-sciences questions are never answered without input from a domain-specialist model. Correctness in the exam domain is enforced by the routing graph, not left to a prompt.
RAG pipeline on LangChain, agent orchestration with LangGraph, and LangSmith for observability across every routed call.
Handles multilingual live-class transcripts (Marathi / Hindi / English); embeddings via gemini-embedding-001 at 768 dimensions on Vertex AI.
Models deployed on Google Cloud Run with NVIDIA L4 GPUs and scale-to-zero, so a coaching academy's budget is not spent on idle GPU hours.
Data minimization by design: logging is deliberately limited to student ID and first name only.

more_projects.title: Azure Foundry Chat
more_projects.description: Deploys a Gemma 3 chat agent on Azure AI Foundry: Bicep-provisioned infrastructure, the model on managed GPU compute, Bing grounding for live web search, and an OpenAI-compatible adapter that registers a managed-compute model as bring-your-own-model. Puts the AI-900 certification to work on real Azure infrastructure.

more_projects.title: Tracechain — Supply Chain Provenance
more_projects.description: Supply chain provenance platform on a 3-tier architecture tracking products, suppliers, and warehouse movements. RESTful APIs over optimized recursive SQL queries retrieve end-to-end product lineage and custody data; React dashboard with real-time analytics and compliance monitoring.

more_projects.title: Course Recommendation App
more_projects.description: Platform for discovering and comparing courses aggregated from Coursera, Udemy, and edX. Express and Prisma ORM over PostgreSQL manage course data, accounts, and reviews; an AI-based recommendation engine and smart search generate suggestions from stated interests and skill goals. Data-sync jobs automated with Cron.

more_projects.role: Built the React frontend and the ML service — Isolation Forest anomaly detection over the cost telemetry.
more_projects.description: Hackathon team project: real-time cost monitoring for a live GCP project — telemetry ingested every five minutes, Isolation Forest anomaly detection, automated remediation of idle VMs and orphan disks, Slack alerts, and a live Socket.IO dashboard.
